Subject: COPPA confirmation and prohibited-use questionnaire

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this — we’re preparing our vendor risk assessment for a new product aimed at 10-13 year olds and need to validate third-party providers who may process data from minors. Please confirm the following for Redwood Inference (hosted API + dedicated options):

1) Does Redwood knowingly target children under 13 or allow customers to target ads or marketing to children via your hosted API?
2) Do you have any age-gating controls or policies at the API/platform level that prevent signups or ingestion of child personal data?
3) For hosted customers, do you allow processing of personal data of minors if a customer claims they have parental consent?
4) Do you accept or process Special Category Data or health-related data under hosted offering?
5) Can you provide evidence: data flow diagram, DPA excerpt referencing restrictions on children’s data, and any attestation/COPPA declaration you can share.

We’ve attached our SIG template (partial) and would appreciate a short attestation or a few-line response by EOD Friday (3/5) so we can move forward with the procurement review.

Thanks,
Samira Patel

KidsLearn Inc

Hi Samira — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below and I’ve attached the documents you requested. I’m looping in Vivek (Product) and Hannah (Legal) for firm confirmation.

1) Targeting: Redwood does not knowingly target children under 13 with our hosted API. Our standard Terms of Service and Acceptable Use Policy prohibit customers from using the hosted API to target or market to children.
2) Age-gating controls: We do not perform identity/age verification for every end-user at the platform level, but we provide customer-facing guidance and sample controls (see attached data-flow map and COPPA-declaration). We also offer Dedicated/Private deployments that customers can configure behind their own identity gates when they need stronger controls.
3) Parental consent: For hosted usage, we require customers to represent and warrant that they have all necessary consents and lawful bases for data they send to the API. We do not independently validate parental consent; customers are responsible for compliance and must not use the hosted API to process known child personal data unless they can meet the applicable legal requirements.
4) Special category / health data: Our hosted API is not intended for processing PHI or special category data. Private deployments (customer-managed VPC/on-prem) can be configured for regulated data with appropriate contractual terms, but hosted customers should not send PHI or protected health information.
5) Evidence attached: COPPA-declaration.pdf (statement of policy), data-flow-map.png (high-level flows for hosted vs dedicated), DPA-excerpt.txt (relevant clauses).

We’ll follow up with a short legal attestation if you need formal signature.

Best,

> Hi Marissa,
> 
> Thanks for taking this — we’re preparing our vendor risk assessment for a new product aimed at 10-13 year olds and need to validate third-party providers who may process data from minors. Please confirm the following for Redwood Inference (hosted API + dedicated options):
> ...

Redwood position (summary):
- Hosted API: Redwood’s hosted service is not marketed to or designed for children under 13. Our contracts and AUP require customers to comply with applicable laws (including COPPA) and to obtain any parental consents necessary. We do not perform platform-level parental consent verification for hosted customers.
- Dedicated/Private: Customers using Dedicated or Private deployments can enforce age-gating at the network/Application level and better isolate data; these options are recommended for regulated or child-facing applications.
- Data minimization & retention: We encourage customers to minimize PII and to use request-scoped TTLs. Our platform supports token-level retention controls and deletion requests per the DPA.
- Subprocessors: Redwood publishes a list of subprocessors and requires flowdown contractual obligations; subprocessors are contractually prohibited from using data for their own purposes.

Requested evidence enclosed: DPA-excerpt.txt (Sections 2.1, 4.3 — customer obligations; processor obligations regarding lawful basis), COPPA-declaration.pdf (policy language we share with customers), and a redacted data-flow diagram.

If you need a signed attestation on company letterhead, please indicate the exact text you need and we’ll route to our Security & Compliance lead for signature.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
